source.locator: Chapter 17, Smells and Heuristics, G25 Magic Numbers
source.paraphrase: A raw number in an expression is a named constant, or one of a few obvious literals.

invariants.why: A bare number forces the next reader to guess the unit and the reason. Naming it, or sticking to an obvious literal, keeps the expression readable.
invariants.fixHint: Bind the number to a named constant, or use 0, 1, -1, 2, 100, or an HTTP status from 100 to 599.
invariants.avoid: The number 1 under a unary minus is the literal -1 and is allowed. A number that is the direct value of a const, let, var, or enum member is the named constant and is allowed; a number inside a larger expression is not. 256 is inside the HTTP range and is allowed. Floats, ports, timeouts, and bit masks outside the list warn. Test files are ignored. This is a literal allowlist, not a judgment that the number is meaningful.

source.paraphrase: Domain behavior has a test the next reader can find next to the code.

invariants.why: A domain file with no nearby test leaves the next change without a place to show the behavior still holds.
invariants.fixHint: Add place.test.ts or place.spec.ts beside the file, under __tests__, or under test/ or tests/ with a src/ prefix mirrored.
invariants.avoid: A test for a different file does not count. place.tests.ts does not count. index.ts and declaration files are excluded because they are barrels, not behavior; a barrel that holds logic is not checked. Under the no-new ratchet, a file that already lacked a test is not newly denied. A new domain file is.

source.paraphrase: A change to an architecture decision record's subject is accompanied by a change to the record.

invariants.why: An architecture file that moves without an ADR change leaves the decision that justified the map out of the same diff.
invariants.fixHint: Change a file under docs/adr in the same diff, or point adr at the directory this project uses. Override paths for the layer map and boundary files this project actually edits.
invariants.avoid: The check looks at path names in the diff, not at whether the ADR text discusses the edit. docs/adr.md and docs/adr-old/ do not match docs/adr/**. A whole-tree audit has no diff, so the check stays quiet. When Git cannot list the working tree, the check stays quiet rather than denying every architecture edit.

source.paraphrase: A TODO or FIXME cites the issue that tracks it.

invariants.why: A TODO with only an owner, or with no reference at all, has no ticket the next reader can open.
invariants.fixHint: Cite #123, a KEY-123 issue id, or a path containing issues/123 or pull/123.
invariants.avoid: This check does not require an owner. vibe-proof/VP-TODO-001 requires an owner and does not require an issue. A comment can fail one and pass the other. HACK and XXX are left to that owner check. The word issue without an id does not count. The check does not ask the tracker whether the issue exists.

source.locator: Chapter 3, Fitness functions and incremental change
source.paraphrase: Risky behavior is reached through a feature flag the change can turn off.

invariants.why: A payments, billing, or checkout module with no flag import can only change by editing the path that is already live.
invariants.fixHint: Import the project's flag module, or override paths and specifiers to the risky globs and the module name this project uses.
invariants.avoid: A file outside the configured globs is not checked. flagstone does not count as flags. A type-only import of the flag module counts. A dynamic import whose specifier is not a string does not. The check does not know whether the flag wraps the risky call.

source.paraphrase: A file that already changes often does not also grow.

invariants.why: A hot file that keeps gaining lines or a longer function becomes the place every later change has to understand.
invariants.fixHint: Move the new behavior to another file, or shrink this file in the same edit. Raise threshold only with a reviewed override.
invariants.avoid: The gate is git rev-list --count HEAD for this path, and it fires only when that count is above threshold. A missing Git answer or a file with no history stays quiet. Non-blank lines and the longest function are the size measures; cyclomatic complexity is not. A new file is not an increase. Blank lines do not count.

source.paraphrase: A function name that says And or Then is doing two things.

invariants.why: And and Then in a function name are a readable sign the function has two jobs.
invariants.fixHint: Split the function so each name is one action.
invariants.avoid: The match is the camel-case words And and Then, not the letters inside handle, random, standard, Candidate, or Android. A const whose value is not a function is not a function name. Test files are ignored. The name can still hide two jobs without those words.
